title: Create authenticated Foundation policy-waiver authority
description:
AUTHORITY-GRANTING FOLLOW-UP split from task-064b97584aff4e07967738f79134a723 after task-e74d3116cbeb4abb96becb08b5896c8e explicitly ruled that Foundation currently has no waiver and no humanApprovalRef mapping.

OBJECTIVE: only after an explicit human product decision, add the authenticated human-approval record, durable writer, strict reader, and validation required to produce a scoped, expiring, SOFT-only PolicyWaiver.

DELIVERABLE: a production human action writes an immutable approval record; the waiver reader joins it to project/principal/action/obligation/scope, rejects expiry or foreign identity, and policy.validate consumes only verified waivers.

NOT IN SCOPE: policy-risk tier classification, autoApprovalOptIns, fabricating humanApprovalRef, waiving HARD obligations or required facts, lifting HOLD_UNKNOWN, or relaxing admission/budget gates.

SAFETY ORDERING: this row is not a prerequisite to delivering the fail-closed resolved-empty waiver behavior in task-064. It is required before any future live non-empty Foundation waiver can be accepted. Keep it BLOCKED until the human authorizes the record and authenticated action.

VERIFICATION COMMAND: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`; the fresh foreground output must contain nonzero Test Files and Tests lines and exit 0.
definitionOfDone: Before source edits, a durable Moe comment records the human-approved approval-record contract, authenticated human action and writer, strict reader, humanApprovalRef derivation, project/principal/action/obligation/scope join keys, expiry semantics, and revocation/supersession rule; absent that decision, the task reports BLOCKED.

Production code creates waiver authority only from an authenticated human action and a durable immutable record; caller-carried waiver fields or approval references are refused before any authority read with exact stable reason code and refusing layer.

The strict reader accepts only unexpired, same-project, same-principal/action, exact-obligation, nonempty-scope, SOFT-only approvals and distinguishes missing, unreadable, stale, revoked, and foreign records without granting authority.
policy.validate consumes the verified waiver reader; resolved-empty remains the result when no approval exists, and no waiver can suppress a HARD obligation, required fact, or HOLD_UNKNOWN.

Focused TDD covers the valid record and every hostile constructibility case, asserts exact code and layer, proves a nonzero generated roster, and includes production mutation drills for expiry, scope, SOFT-only, and humanApprovalRef binding.
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` runs standalone in the foreground, exits 0, and prints nonzero Test Files and Tests counts; `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` also exits 0.

comments.author: architect-dba58d99
comments.content:
HUMAN DECISION PROPOSAL — NOT YET AUTHORITY (architect-dba58d99, HEAD 88218d962d2c3c82b63ff19befdad05358fd4660, 2026-08-30).

Fresh measurements: resolvePolicyWaivers() is still zero-argument RESOLVED_EMPTY at policy-fact-resolver.ts:29 and has one production caller, bootstrap-policy-services.ts:162. Caller input.waivers already refuses BOOTSTRAP_POLICY_WAIVER_UNVERIFIABLE / DAEMON_INGRESS before reads, but caller approvalRef/humanApprovalRef/waiverRef extras are currently silently ignored and must gain an exact pre-read fence. Core applies a waiver only to a dropped SOFT obligation; HARD loss and required-fact shrink never consult waivers, and HOLD_UNKNOWN dominates. Authoritative design lines 699/708/710/712/1007 make this R3, reason-required, step-up, and a distinct typed approval.decide arm. Current approval records have no obligation/scope/expiry/revocation and may not be repurposed.

RECOMMENDED CONTRACT A (the requested six decisions):
1. ACTION — add an HTTP/control-room-only, MCP-excluded, ADMIN-capability typed approval.decide arm with decisionKind=SOFT_POLICY_WAIVER and operation GRANT|REVOKE. It is self-bound: configured operator/durably authenticated HUMAN signer is also the policy.validate principal; no delegation in v1. Require a nonempty reason and consume one fresh server-derived step-up reference. This explicitly treats the existing one-shot HTTP human-review/step-up burn as Foundation v1 step-up; real MFA/WebAuthn would instead be a prerequisite.
2. IMMUTABLE RECORD — append PolicyWaiverGranted.v1 with exact canonical fields: actionKind, approvedAt, approvedBy, commandId, decisionReason, expiresAtEpochMs, humanApprovalRef, namedObligationId, policyRevisionRef, projectId, canonical scope, stepUpAuthRef, supersedesWaiverRef|null, waiverRef. REVOKE appends PolicyWaiverRevoked.v1 against the same server-derived authority tuple; it never mutates the grant. The command may name semantic intent (action/policy/obligation/scope/expiry) but may not carry either ref.
3. REFS — humanApprovalRef = approval:policy-waiver:sha256:<domain-separated SHA-256 of the canonical immutable decision material, including authenticated project/principal, command identity, decidedAt, reason and step-up, excluding the ref>. waiverRef = policy-waiver:sha256:<domain-separated SHA-256 of humanApprovalRef plus the exact authority tuple>. Both are recomputed by the reader.
4. JOINS/SCOPE — exact project, approvedBy==authenticated policy.validate principal, exact action, exact installed policyRevisionRef, namedObligationId resolving uniquely to SOFT (ambiguous or any HARD occurrence refuses), and sorted/unique/nonempty scope SET-EQUALITY. This deliberately prevents core's weaker subset predicate from broadening authority.
5. EXPIRY — human supplies an explicit canonical UTC expiry; no default. It must be > daemon decidedAt and <= decidedAt+24h, with exclusive validity (expired at equality), no grace or renewal. A policy-revision change is stale.
6. REVOCATION/SUPERSESSION — REVOKE resolves the current grant by the same exact tuple and appends a tombstone. A later GRANT for that tuple atomically supersedes the prior waiver and records its ref; optimistic expected-version fencing rejects races. policy.validate also carries a read-only expected-version leg for every consumed waiver aggregate so revoke-after-read cannot race into a durable ALLOW.

Reader refusals stay fail-closed and distinct at DAEMON_POLICY_WAIVER: RECORD_MISSING, RECORD_UNREADABLE, EXPIRED, REVOKED, SUPERSEDED, PROJECT_FOREIGN, PRINCIPAL_FOREIGN, ACTION_FOREIGN, POLICY_STALE, OBLIGATION_FOREIGN, SCOPE_FOREIGN, NOT_SOFT. No verified record => RESOLVED_EMPTY.

ALTERNATIVES requiring an explicit different ruling: B) permit a separately named beneficiary principal (larger delegated authority; recommend max 4h and session/capability joins), or C) create policy.waiver.grant|revoke operator-only commands (simpler decoders but amends design line 1007). Also, if the existing one-shot step-up burn is not acceptable as R3 authentication, this row must depend on a real re-auth producer.

Scope warning: approval-intent/registry sources are already 244/358 lines and the integration reader is a separate five-file consumer slice. After approval I will SPIDR the action/writer from the strict reader/integration rather than exceed the plan/file caps.
